name: Laryngoplasty / Adam's apple surgery

lead: Chondrolaryngoplasty, popularly called a tracheal shave, trims the thyroid cartilage to flatten a prominent Adam's apple and smooth the front of the neck. It is among the more common surgeries for transgender women and is also sought by others who want a less prominent Adam's apple.

A surgeon makes a small incision and shaves the cartilage, sometimes endoscopically through the chin or mouth. The result is directly visible, and Wikipedia reports most patients are satisfied, with complaints mostly about residual prominence or scarring. It was first described in 1975.

paras: It is done by a surgeon as a short procedure, with about two weeks of recovery. The voice is usually unaffected.

The vocal folds sit close to the cartilage, so rare damage and slight pitch changes are reported. Swelling, bruising and temporary swallowing difficulty are common during recovery, and scarring is possible.

angle.text: Chondrolaryngoplasty shaves the thyroid cartilage so the Adam's apple looks flatter and the neck front smoother, often sought for a more feminine contour. The change is visible right away, and published series report mostly satisfied patients.

lead: Chondrolaryngoplasty, popularly called a tracheal shave, reduces the thyroid cartilage that forms the Adam's apple. The nickname is a misnomer because the trachea is not involved.[1]

It is among the more common surgeries for transgender women and is also sought by others uncomfortable with a prominent Adam's apple.[1] It was first described by Francis G. Wolfort and Richard G. Parry in 1975.[1] The voice is usually unaffected, though slight pitch changes have been reported.[1]

paras: Under local or general anesthesia, a surgeon makes a small incision, often placed in a skin fold, and shaves the protruding cartilage. Newer variants hide the incision under the chin or inside the mouth and may be endoscopic.[1]

Because the vocal folds lie close to the site, they can rarely be damaged. Swelling, bruising and temporary difficulty swallowing or speaking are common.[1] Most patients are satisfied; dissatisfaction most often concerns remaining prominence or a visible scar.[1] Feminization laryngoplasty is a different procedure that can affect voice.[1]

timeline.event: Technique described by Wolfort and Parry.[1]
